dedupe_keys.name: openmines open pit mine truck dispatching simulation environment

description: A light open-source simulator of truck haulage in an open-pit mine. The GitHub README says OpenMines is a lightweight mining simulation environment for studying truck dispatching, with a Gymnasium environment so that reinforcement learning and rule-based dispatch algorithms can be trained and compared. The work was presented at IEEE IV 2024 and is described in arXiv paper 2404.00622 by Shi Meng and co-authors. The code is free to download under the MIT licence. Coverage is a configurable mine layout, not a real site. Caveats: loaders, dumps and road layouts are set by the user, and the page read does not give validation against a real mine. For simulation it lets users test how haulage throughput drops when trucks, loaders or haul roads are lost, and how dispatch rules recover production, a building block for mine operations resilience studies. A related catalogue record is the GoldSim mine water and waste record.
